categories.name: Idea & Problem
categories.question: Is the problem real and painful? Who exactly has it?

anchors.3: Vague problem, no clear sufferer, or solution looking for a problem.
anchors.5: Recognizable problem for a named audience; pain is plausible but unproven.
anchors.7: Clear ICP, painful job-to-be-done, evidence from users/store/reviews or domain knowledge with sources.
anchors.9: Narrow, urgent problem with named competitors and proof people already pay or churn without a fix.

categories.name: Differentiation
categories.question: Why this over what exists? Is it generic?

anchors.3: Feature-parity clone; no named reason to switch.
anchors.5: One real angle (niche, UX, price, platform) but easy to copy or weakly communicated.
anchors.7: Clear, defensible difference vs at least 3 named competitors with sources.
anchors.9: Hard-to-copy wedge (data, workflow lock-in, distribution, unique IP) proven against named peers.

categories.name: Revenue Model
categories.question: Is there a believable path to money for this product and this creator?

anchors.3: No model, or model the creator cannot collect (payments/region), or ads-only with no placement plan.
anchors.5: A model exists (ads/IAP/sub) but unit economics or fit are hand-wavy.
anchors.7: Model fits audience and creator constraints; placement/pricing/consent sketched with evidence.
anchors.9: Credible ceiling math with labeled assumptions; model matches comparable products with sources.

categories.name: UI & Visual Design
categories.question: Color, contrast, type, spacing, hierarchy, consistency

anchors.3: Clashing palette, illegible text, inconsistent components; looks unfinished.
anchors.5: Readable and consistent enough to ship; few hierarchy or density issues.
anchors.7: Tight system: palette, type scale, spacing, one primary action; AA contrast on reviewed screens.
anchors.9: Polished, distinctive visual language that still meets accessibility and consistency checks.

categories.name: UX & Onboarding
categories.question: Time to first value, friction, flows, states

anchors.3: Long path to value; permission walls; missing empty/error/offline states.
anchors.5: User can reach core value with some friction; main happy path works.
anchors.7: Fast first value, clear flows, good empty/loading/error coverage on reviewed paths.
anchors.9: Onboarding and recovery paths feel intentional; friction is justified and measured.

categories.name: Retention & Engagement
categories.question: Why would anyone come back? Is there a loop?

anchors.3: One-shot utility; no reason or reminder to return.
anchors.5: A loop exists (habit, content, progress, social) but weak or unmeasured.
anchors.7: Clear return loop with triggers (notifications, streaks, new content) backed by code or metrics.
anchors.9: Loop + proof (retention metrics or strong engagement design) vs comparable products.

categories.name: Growth & Distribution
categories.question: Store listing / SEO, channels, virality, shareability

anchors.3: Weak listing/SEO, no channels, nothing shareable.
anchors.5: Basic listing or landing page; one plausible channel.
anchors.7: Strong listing/SEO assets, clear channels, some share or referral surface.
anchors.9: Listing + channels + measurable conversion or virality with sourced evidence.

categories.name: Technical Quality
categories.question: Architecture, performance, tests, security (from the codebase)

anchors.3: Fragile structure, secrets in repo, no tests, obvious perf footguns.
anchors.5: Readable architecture for the stage; some tests or crash reporting; no glaring secrets.
anchors.7: Consistent patterns, meaningful tests, release hygiene, basic security hygiene.
anchors.9: Strong architecture and observability for the product stage; evidence of perf/reliability work.

categories.name: Trust & Compliance
categories.question: Privacy policy, permissions, store policy, consent, data safety

anchors.3: Missing privacy policy, over-broad permissions, no consent where required.
anchors.5: Policy and permissions present; some gaps vs data collected.
anchors.7: Policy, consent, permissions, and data-safety claims align with code.
anchors.9: Tight alignment plus store-policy awareness with evidence (listings, SDK config, consent UI).

categories.name: Polish & Store Readiness
categories.question: Completeness, bugs, edge cases, ready to ship?

anchors.3: Placeholder copy, broken edges, not shippable.
anchors.5: Core flows work; rough edges remain; maybe soft-launchable.
anchors.7: Store assets ready, edge cases handled on reviewed paths, release config sane.
anchors.9: Ship-ready with strong store assets and few open critical/major findings.
